variants.headline: Looking back: party leader faces a public scandal
variants.sub: The leader of {party}, {leader}, is the subject of a newly revealed scandal.
variants.body:
We return to {first_reported}. Our report recorded this: A scandal concerning {leader}, the leader of {party}, had come to light.

The gazette confines its factual account to the revelation of the scandal. A political embarrassment and a finding under law are distinct matters. The public record is best served by keeping the distinction clear and by avoiding particulars which have not been supplied to this newspaper.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

This paper treats {target} as a subject for scrutiny, while withholding conclusions the reported revelation does not establish. Attention to trust need not depend upon an invented account of wrongdoing.

variants.headline: Looking back: leadership under an unwelcome spotlight
variants.sub: A scandal about {leader}, leader of {party}, has become public.

Time changes the distance from an event, not the need to judge it carefully. Any claim about improvement or deterioration needs more than a recollection of the original news.
